title: identity.email.send.v1
description: The payload of an email-send event, derived from the three OutboxEventType constructors. The event_type name is the version; the payload shape is owned by that version. No Rust type in the repository carries this payload's shape today — only the event_type string exists — so this is a PROMISE for the producer that Phase 7 builds, not a description of a type that exists.
x-rust-type: NONE — the event_type string exists (OutboxEventType::email_send_v1); no payload struct exists
x-serde-status: the event_type is IMPLEMENTED; the payload is NOT. OutboxEventType::email_send_v1() returns this name. A producer that writes this payload does not exist yet.

kind.description: Which email. At minimum a password-reset, email-verification, and security-notification variant. The exact set is the producer's to fix in Phase 7.
kind.x-not-a-contract: This enum is deliberately left open. Writing a closed list here would be a claim about types that do not exist. Phase 7 fixes it and this schema is updated in the same commit.

user_id.description: The user the email is for, when the email is about a known account.

token.description: A single-use token embedded in the email, when the email carries one. The token is not an outbox id; it has its own lifecycle and its own expiry.

expires_at_ms.description: When the token in this email expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

x-consumption.idempotency: keyed on the outbox event id (QueuedEvent.id), never on the payload. Two sends of the same email content are two facts and must both be delivered.
x-consumption.refusal: a consumer that cannot recognise the type refuses the message rather than guessing at the shape
x-consumption.disposition: BatchOutcome::Done, Retry, or DeadLetter — three named outcomes, no 'silently ignored'
